title: Candidate 48 quadratic response splits both seeded Lorentz vectors 2+2

claim.statement: The canonical candidate-48 vacuum does not admit a direct SO(5)-equivariant quadratic extension from either seeded SO(4) vector sector, because each four-vector Hessian block is anisotropic.
claim.retainedStructure: The adjoint-10 and symmetric-traceless-14 seed sectors are mutually orthogonal in both the field Gram form and Hessian, and have identical spectra.

setup.method: Project the original 102-coordinate scalar span into each completed-module SO(4) vector, take the field-Gram metric-adjoint image as its canonical seed preimage, and restrict the exact candidate-48 Hessian.

interpretation: The exact 2+2 degeneracy is consistent with residual symmetry smaller than Lorentz SO(4), rather than numerical instability.
Absence of 10-to-14 mixing satisfies one necessary Schur condition, but isotropy within each SO(4) vector fails.
Any full SO(5) quadratic completion must either change/average the vacuum, add symmetry-restoring response terms, or accept spontaneous Lorentz breaking.
falsifiers: The no-go is overturned if a field-Gram-equivalent seed embedding yields scalar four-by-four Hessian blocks.
A moduli or compact-orbit average that remains a legitimate single-vacuum local theory and makes both blocks scalar would evade the fixed-vacuum obstruction.
The result does not test Hessian coefficients on the unseeded 6, 1, and 9 descendants; passing seed isotropy would still be only necessary, not sufficient.
nextBranches: Sample the candidate-48 finite moduli and average the transported seed Hessians.
Resolve the 2+2 eigenspaces under the canonical U(1) stabilizer.
Test minimal symmetry-restoring counterterms constrained to vanish on the certified radial KKT data.
